text:
Dylan Garand spent three seasons in Hartford waiting for a real look, and the 2020 fourth-rounder is getting one now: 13 appearances, 12 starts and a 6-6-1 record. The bigger sign is underneath. He has saved 2.23 goals above expected (goals saved above expected measures saves beyond what the quality of shots predicts), and he has stopped 86% of high-danger shots, 84th percentile in the league, against a league rate of 81%.

The net around him is shifting too. The New York Post's Mollie Walker reported that James Reimer was placed on waivers as the next step in Joonas Korpisalo's impending return, and Markerzone framed it as a bigger question behind Garand. Our read: Korpisalo coming back changes who sits on the bench more than who starts, as long as Garand keeps this up.

The honest caveat is the range. Our talent estimate puts his true save rate around .890, roughly league average, with this start at the hot end of it. His last five starts netted almost exactly zero above expected (0.06), so the early edge has flattened. We'd watch whether the high-danger saves hold, because that is where his case lives.
headline: Garand has the Rangers' net, and the job looks real
